title: Does Verbalized Sampling Break Safety-Relevant Homogeneity?

original_idea.body:
# Does Verbalized Sampling Break Safety-Relevant Homogeneity?

**Problem:** Verbalized Sampling mitigates mode collapse on creative tasks. Whether it diversifies SAFETY-relevant outputs across models - and whether diversified responses include MORE unsafe ones - is unknown.

**Direction:** Apply VS prompting to open models on a safety-relevant slice. Compare inter-model homogeneity with vs without, and rubric-check whether diversified outputs introduce unsafe content. Quantify the diversity-vs-safety tradeoff.

**Why it matters:** If diversity-promoting methods re-introduce unsafe modes the cure has hidden costs. Training-free prompting, lab-independent.

**Relevant context:** Verbalized Sampling (arXiv:2510.01171); Artificial Hivemind diversity-objectives open problem.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible: testing whether a proposed monoculture fix re-introduces unsafe modes; useful but indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt-only, training-free, plus rubric-based safety check; accessible with a mentor for rubric design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused with/without VS comparison plus a safety-content audit; clear deliverable.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Training-free, public models; evaluates a mitigation labs underprioritize externally.

novelty.reasoning: VS is recent; its inter-model safety effect untested, partly novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: VS demonstrated on creative tasks; safety/inter-model effect is an open extension.
